elements.name: Hydrogen
elements.description: The lightest element, forming the building blocks of water and organic molecules.
elements.historicalFacts: Identified by Henry Cavendish in 1766 and named by Antoine Lavoisier.

elements.name: Helium
elements.description: A noble gas famed for its low density and use in cryogenics.
elements.historicalFacts: First observed in the solar spectrum in 1868 by Jules Janssen and Norman Lockyer.

elements.name: Lithium
elements.description: A soft, silvery alkali metal essential in rechargeable batteries.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered in 1817 by Johan August Arfwedson in the mineral petalite.

elements.name: Beryllium
elements.description: A hard, brittle metal used in aerospace for its stiffness and low density.
elements.historicalFacts: Identified as an element in 1798 by Louis Nicolas Vauquelin.

elements.name: Boron
elements.description: A metalloid vital for glassmaking and semiconductor technology.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated in 1808 independently by Humphry Davy and by Gay-Lussac with Thénard.

elements.name: Carbon
elements.description: An essential element of life with allotropes like diamond and graphite.
elements.historicalFacts: Known since antiquity in forms such as charcoal and diamond.

elements.name: Nitrogen
elements.description: A diatomic gas forming 78% of Earth's atmosphere and vital to biomolecules.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated by Daniel Rutherford in 1772.

elements.name: Oxygen
elements.description: A life-sustaining gas essential for respiration and combustion.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered independently by Carl Scheele and Joseph Priestley in the 1770s.

elements.name: Fluorine
elements.description: The most electronegative element, forming strong bonds and reactive compounds.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated by Henri Moissan in 1886 using electrolysis.

elements.name: Neon
elements.description: A noble gas known for its bright orange-red glow in neon lights.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered in 1898 by William Ramsay and Morris Travers.

elements.name: Sodium
elements.description: A reactive alkali metal that forms salts and is essential for nerve function.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated by Humphry Davy in 1807 via electrolysis of molten sodium hydroxide.

elements.name: Magnesium
elements.description: A lightweight structural metal vital for chlorophyll and aerospace alloys.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated by Humphry Davy in 1808 from magnesium oxide.

elements.name: Aluminium
elements.description: A lightweight, corrosion-resistant metal used extensively in transportation.
elements.historicalFacts: First produced in pure form by Hans Christian Ørsted in 1825.

elements.name: Silicon
elements.description: A semiconductor cornerstone used in electronics and solar cells.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated by Jöns Jakob Berzelius in 1824.

elements.name: Phosphorus
elements.description: An essential nutrient with reactive allotropes like white and red phosphorus.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Hennig Brand in 1669 while distilling urine.

elements.name: Sulfur
elements.description: A yellow non-metal crucial for proteins and sulfuric acid production.
elements.historicalFacts: Known since antiquity and referenced in many ancient texts.

elements.name: Chlorine
elements.description: A greenish halogen used for disinfection and PVC production.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated by Carl Wilhelm Scheele in 1774, later named by Humphry Davy.

elements.name: Argon
elements.description: An inert noble gas used in lighting and shielding gas for welding.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Lord Rayleigh and William Ramsay in 1894.

elements.name: Potassium
elements.description: A highly reactive metal vital for biological processes.
elements.historicalFacts: First isolated by Humphry Davy in 1807 from potash.

elements.name: Calcium
elements.description: An alkaline earth metal critical for bones and shell formation.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated by Humphry Davy in 1808 from lime.

elements.name: Scandium
elements.description: A lightweight transition metal used in aerospace alloys and lighting.
elements.historicalFacts: Predicted by Dmitri Mendeleev and discovered by Lars Fredrik Nilson in 1879.

elements.name: Titanium
elements.description: A strong, corrosion-resistant metal used in aerospace and implants.
elements.historicalFacts: Identified by William Gregor in 1791 and named by Martin Heinrich Klaproth.

elements.name: Vanadium
elements.description: A tough metal used to strengthen steel and in catalysts.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Andrés Manuel del Río in 1801 and rediscovered in 1830 by Nils Sefström.

elements.name: Chromium
elements.description: A hard, lustrous metal used in plating and stainless steel.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered in 1797 by Louis Nicolas Vauquelin in crocoite ore.

elements.name: Manganese
elements.description: An element crucial in steelmaking and biological enzymes.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated by Johan Gottlieb Gahn in 1774 by reducing manganese dioxide.

elements.name: Iron
elements.description: A ubiquitous structural metal central to hemoglobin and industry.
elements.historicalFacts: Known since antiquity, ushering in the Iron Age around 1200 BCE.

elements.name: Cobalt
elements.description: A ferromagnetic metal used in superalloys and rechargeable batteries.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated by Georg Brandt around 1735 while investigating blue pigments.

elements.name: Nickel
elements.description: A corrosion-resistant metal used in alloys and catalysts.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated in 1751 by Axel Fredrik Cronstedt from niccolite ore.

elements.name: Copper
elements.description: A conductive metal used in wiring, coins, and antimicrobial surfaces.
elements.historicalFacts: Known since ancient times; the name derives from Cyprus.

elements.name: Zinc
elements.description: A metal used in galvanization, alloys, and biological enzymes.
elements.historicalFacts: Recognized as a distinct metal in India around the 12th century.

elements.name: Gallium
elements.description: A metal that melts in the hand, used in semiconductors and LEDs.
elements.historicalFacts: Predicted by Mendeleev and discovered by Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran in 1875.

elements.name: Germanium
elements.description: A gray metalloid used in fiber optics and infrared optics.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Clemens Winkler in 1886, confirming Mendeleev's eka-silicon.

elements.name: Arsenic
elements.description: A toxic metalloid used in pesticides, semiconductors, and wood preservation.
elements.historicalFacts: Known since ancient times; used as a poison in antiquity.

elements.name: Selenium
elements.description: A non-metal with photoconductive properties used in electronics.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Jöns Jakob Berzelius in 1817.

elements.name: Bromine
elements.description: A reddish-brown liquid halogen used in flame retardants and photography.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered independently by Antoine Balard and Carl Löwig in 1825.

elements.name: Krypton
elements.description: A noble gas used in lighting and high-speed photography.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by William Ramsay and Morris Travers in 1898.

elements.name: Rubidium
elements.description: A highly reactive alkali metal used in research and specialty glasses.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Robert Bunsen and Gustav Kirchhoff in 1861 via spectroscopy.

elements.name: Strontium
elements.description: A reactive earth metal used in fireworks and medical imaging.
elements.historicalFacts: Identified in strontianite ore in 1790 by Adair Crawford.

elements.name: Yttrium
elements.description: A silvery transition metal used in phosphors and superconductors.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Johan Gadolin in 1794 in Ytterby, Sweden.

elements.name: Zirconium
elements.description: A corrosion-resistant metal used in nuclear reactors and ceramics.
elements.historicalFacts: First isolated in 1824 by Jöns Jakob Berzelius from zircon.

elements.name: Niobium
elements.description: A ductile metal used in superconductors and high-strength alloys.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Charles Hatchett in 1801; once confused with tantalum.

elements.name: Molybdenum
elements.description: A refractory metal essential for high-strength steel and enzymes.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated in 1781 by Peter Jacob Hjelm from molybdenite.

elements.name: Technetium
elements.description: The first artificially produced element, used in medical diagnostics.
elements.historicalFacts: Synthesized in 1937 by Carlo Perrier and Emilio Segrè; naturally occurring only in trace amounts.

elements.name: Ruthenium
elements.description: A rare platinum-group metal used in electronics and catalysts.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Karl Ernst Claus in 1844 from Ural platinum ores.

elements.name: Rhodium
elements.description: A reflective precious metal used in catalytic converters and jewelry plating.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by William Hyde Wollaston in 1803 along with palladium.

elements.name: Palladium
elements.description: A precious metal valued for catalysis and hydrogen absorption.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by William Hyde Wollaston in 1803 and named after the asteroid Pallas.

elements.name: Silver
elements.description: A precious, highly conductive metal used in jewelry and electronics.
elements.historicalFacts: Known since antiquity; used in currencies and ornamental objects.

elements.name: Cadmium
elements.description: A soft metal primarily used in batteries and pigments.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Friedrich Stromeyer in 1817 as an impurity in zinc oxide.

elements.name: Indium
elements.description: A soft metal used in touchscreens and low-melting alloys.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Ferdinand Reich and Hieronymous Richter in 1863 via spectroscopy.

elements.name: Tin
elements.description: A malleable metal used in solder, coatings, and bronze.
elements.historicalFacts: Known since ancient times; central to the Bronze Age when alloyed with copper.

elements.name: Antimony
elements.description: A metalloid used in flame retardants, alloys, and semiconductors.
elements.historicalFacts: Known since antiquity; used by ancient Egyptians in cosmetics.

elements.name: Tellurium
elements.description: A brittle metalloid used in thermoelectrics and metallurgy.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Franz-Joseph Müller von Reichenstein in 1782 and named by Martin Klaproth.

elements.name: Iodine
elements.description: A dark violet halogen essential for thyroid hormones.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Bernard Courtois in 1811 from seaweed ash.

elements.name: Xenon
elements.description: A heavy noble gas used in lighting and anesthesia.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by William Ramsay and Morris Travers in 1898 in liquefied air.

elements.name: Cesium
elements.description: A soft, highly reactive metal central to atomic clocks.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Robert Bunsen and Gustav Kirchhoff via spectroscopy in 1860.

elements.name: Barium
elements.description: A dense metal used in contrast agents and spark plugs.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated by Humphry Davy in 1808 by electrolysis of molten baryta.

elements.name: Lanthanum
elements.description: A soft rare-earth metal used in optics and rechargeable batteries.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Carl Gustaf Mosander in 1839 while analyzing cerium salts.

elements.name: Cerium
elements.description: A versatile rare-earth element used in catalysts and polishing powders.
elements.historicalFacts: Identified by Martin Heinrich Klaproth, Jöns Berzelius, and Wilhelm Hisinger in 1803.

elements.name: Praseodymium
elements.description: A rare-earth metal used in magnets and specialized glasses.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated in 1885 by Carl Auer von Welsbach from didymium.

elements.name: Neodymium
elements.description: A rare-earth metal essential for high-performance magnets.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered alongside praseodymium in 1885 by Carl Auer von Welsbach.

elements.name: Promethium
elements.description: A radioactive rare-earth metal used in luminescent paints and nuclear batteries.
elements.historicalFacts: First produced in 1945 by Jacob A. Marinsky, Lawrence E. Glendenin, and Charles D. Coryell.

elements.name: Samarium
elements.description: A rare-earth element used in permanent magnets and cancer therapy.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Paul Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran in 1879.

elements.name: Europium
elements.description: A rare-earth element valued for its red and blue phosphors in displays.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated by Eugène-Anatole Demarçay in 1901.

elements.name: Gadolinium
elements.description: A rare-earth metal with remarkable neutron absorption and magnetic properties.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Jean Charles Galissard de Marignac in 1880.

elements.name: Terbium
elements.description: A rare-earth element used in green phosphors and fuel cells.
elements.historicalFacts: Identified in 1843 by Carl Gustaf Mosander while studying yttrium.

elements.name: Dysprosium
elements.description: A rare-earth metal with high magnetic susceptibility used in magnets.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Paul Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran in 1886.

elements.name: Holmium
elements.description: A rare-earth element with high magnetic strength and neutron absorption.
elements.historicalFacts: Identified by Per Teodor Cleve in 1878.

elements.name: Erbium
elements.description: A rare-earth element used in fiber optics and lasers.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Carl Gustaf Mosander in 1843.

elements.name: Thulium
elements.description: A scarce rare-earth element used in portable X-ray devices and lasers.
elements.historicalFacts: Identified by Per Teodor Cleve in 1879 as part of erbia fractions.

elements.name: Ytterbium
elements.description: A rare-earth metal used in fiber lasers and atomic clocks.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Jean Charles Galissard de Marignac in 1878.

elements.name: Lutetium
elements.description: A dense rare-earth metal used in catalysts and positron emission tomography.
elements.historicalFacts: Named by Georges Urbain in 1907 after Lutetia, the Roman name for Paris.

elements.name: Hafnium
elements.description: A corrosion-resistant metal used in nuclear reactors and electronics.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Georg von Hevesy and Dirk Coster in 1923 in zirconium ores.

elements.name: Tantalum
elements.description: A highly corrosion-resistant metal used in electronics and implants.
elements.historicalFacts: Identified by Anders Ekeberg in 1802; named after the Greek myth of Tantalus.

elements.name: Tungsten
elements.description: A refractory metal with the highest melting point, used in filaments and tools.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated from wolframite by the Elhuyar brothers in 1783.

elements.name: Rhenium
elements.description: A dense metal used in high-temperature superalloys and catalysts.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered in 1925 by Ida and Walter Noddack and Otto Berg.

elements.name: Osmium
elements.description: The densest naturally occurring element, used in pens and catalysts.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Smithson Tennant in 1803 alongside iridium.

elements.name: Iridium
elements.description: A dense, corrosion-resistant metal used in spark plugs and catalysts.
elements.historicalFacts: Also discovered by Smithson Tennant in 1803 in platinum ores.

elements.name: Platinum
elements.description: A precious metal prized for its stability and catalytic properties.
elements.historicalFacts: Known to pre-Columbian South Americans; introduced to Europe in the 18th century.

elements.name: Gold
elements.description: A noble metal renowned for its corrosion resistance and conductivity.
elements.historicalFacts: Used by human civilizations for millennia as a symbol of wealth.

elements.name: Mercury
elements.description: A liquid metal at room temperature used in thermometers and switches.
elements.historicalFacts: Known since ancient times; called quicksilver by alchemists.

elements.name: Thallium
elements.description: A toxic heavy metal used in electronics and specialized glass.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by William Crookes in 1861 via spectroscopy of selenium ores.

elements.name: Lead
elements.description: A dense, malleable metal used historically in plumbing and batteries.
elements.historicalFacts: Known since antiquity; extensively used by Romans for pipes and pigments.

elements.name: Bismuth
elements.description: A brittle metal with low toxicity used in cosmetics and pharmaceuticals.
elements.historicalFacts: Known since the Middle Ages; often confused with lead and tin.

elements.name: Polonium
elements.description: A highly radioactive element used in neutron sources and anti-static devices.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Marie and Pierre Curie in 1898; named after Poland.

elements.name: Astatine
elements.description: An extremely rare radioactive halogen with limited practical applications.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered in 1940 by Dale Corson, Kenneth MacKenzie, and Emilio Segrè.

elements.name: Radon
elements.description: A radioactive noble gas that can accumulate in homes from soil.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered in 1899 by Ernest Rutherford and Robert B. Owens as a decay product.

elements.name: Francium
elements.description: An extremely rare, radioactive alkali metal with no commercial uses.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Marguerite Perey in 1939 at the Curie Institute.

elements.name: Radium
elements.description: A highly radioactive alkaline earth metal once used in luminous paints.
elements.historicalFacts: Isolated by Marie and Pierre Curie in 1898 from pitchblende.

elements.name: Actinium
elements.description: A radioactive metal that marks the start of the actinide series.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Friedrich O. Giesel in 1899 and by André-Louis Debierne in 1899.

elements.name: Thorium
elements.description: A fertile nuclear material considered for advanced reactor fuel.
elements.historicalFacts: Identified by Jöns Jakob Berzelius in 1828 and named after Thor.

elements.name: Protactinium
elements.description: A rare actinide used for scientific research and nuclear studies.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Oswald Helmuth Göhring and Kasimir Fajans in 1913; named by Otto Hahn and Lise Meitner.

elements.name: Uranium
elements.description: A heavy actinide used as fuel in nuclear reactors and weapons.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered by Martin Heinrich Klaproth in 1789; named after the planet Uranus.

elements.name: Neptunium
elements.description: A radioactive actinide produced in reactors, used in neutron detectors.
elements.historicalFacts: First synthesized in 1940 by Edwin McMillan and Philip Abelson.

elements.name: Plutonium
elements.description: A fissile actinide central to nuclear weapons and mixed oxide fuel.
elements.historicalFacts: Synthesized in 1940 by Glenn T. Seaborg, Edwin M. McMillan, Joseph W. Kennedy, and Arthur Wahl.

elements.name: Americium
elements.description: A synthetic actinide used in smoke detectors and neutron sources.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered in 1944 by Glenn T. Seaborg and colleagues during Manhattan Project research.

elements.name: Curium
elements.description: A heavy actinide used in power sources for space missions.
elements.historicalFacts: Produced in 1944 by Seaborg's team; named after Marie and Pierre Curie.

elements.name: Berkelium
elements.description: A synthetic actinide used only in scientific research.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered in 1949 at UC Berkeley by Thompson, Street, Ghiorso, and Seaborg.

elements.name: Californium
elements.description: A strong neutron emitter used in neutron radiography and startup of reactors.
elements.historicalFacts: Synthesized in 1950 at UC Berkeley; named after California.

elements.name: Einsteinium
elements.description: A synthetic element discovered in hydrogen bomb debris.
elements.historicalFacts: Identified in 1952 following the first thermonuclear explosion; named after Albert Einstein.

elements.name: Fermium
elements.description: A synthetic actinide formed in nuclear explosions; used solely for research.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered alongside einsteinium in 1952 thermonuclear debris; named after Enrico Fermi.

elements.name: Mendelevium
elements.description: A synthetic actinide named after Dmitri Mendeleev.
elements.historicalFacts: First synthesized in 1955 by Seaborg and coworkers using the 60-inch cyclotron.

elements.name: Nobelium
elements.description: A synthetic actinide named after Alfred Nobel.
elements.historicalFacts: Confirmed in 1957 by the Nobel Institute in Sweden and later at Berkeley.

elements.name: Lawrencium
elements.description: A synthetic element marking the end of the actinide series.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered in 1961 at Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory.

elements.name: Rutherfordium
elements.description: A synthetic transactinide studied for its chemistry analogous to hafnium.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered in 1964 at Dubna and confirmed at Berkeley; named after Ernest Rutherford.

elements.name: Dubnium
elements.description: A synthetic element named after Dubna, Russia.
elements.historicalFacts: Co-discovered by teams in Dubna and Berkeley in the late 1960s.

elements.name: Seaborgium
elements.description: A transactinide element named to honor Glenn T. Seaborg.
elements.historicalFacts: Synthesized in 1974 at the Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory.

elements.name: Bohrium
elements.description: A synthetic element named after Niels Bohr.
elements.historicalFacts: Produced in 1981 by a German team at GSI Helmholtz Centre.

elements.name: Hassium
elements.description: A transactinide expected to behave like osmium.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered in 1984 by the GSI team in Darmstadt, Germany.

elements.name: Meitnerium
elements.description: A synthetic element named after Lise Meitner.
elements.historicalFacts: Synthesized in 1982 at GSI by bombarding bismuth with iron ions.

elements.name: Darmstadtium
elements.description: A synthetic element named after Darmstadt, Germany.
elements.historicalFacts: First created in 1994 by the GSI team via nickel bombardment.

elements.name: Roentgenium
elements.description: A synthetic element named in honor of Wilhelm Röntgen.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered in 1994 at GSI through bismuth-gold fusion.

elements.name: Copernicium
elements.description: A volatile transactinide named after Nicolaus Copernicus.
elements.historicalFacts: First synthesized in 1996 at GSI; exhibits noble gas-like volatility.

elements.name: Nihonium
elements.description: A synthetic p-block element named after Japan (Nihon).
elements.historicalFacts: First synthesized in 2004 by RIKEN in Japan; confirmed in 2012.

elements.name: Flerovium
elements.description: A superheavy element exhibiting possible noble-metal behavior.
elements.historicalFacts: Synthesized in 1998 at the Flerov Laboratory in Dubna.

elements.name: Moscovium
elements.description: A synthetic element named after Moscow Oblast.
elements.historicalFacts: Created jointly by Dubna and Livermore scientists in 2003.

elements.name: Livermorium
elements.description: A synthetic element named after Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory.
elements.historicalFacts: Created in 2000 by joint efforts of Dubna and Livermore scientists.

elements.name: Tennessine
elements.description: A synthetic halogen named for the state of Tennessee.
elements.historicalFacts: Synthesized in 2010 by a Russian–American collaboration.

elements.name: Oganesson
elements.description: The heaviest noble gas, predicted to have unusual properties.
elements.historicalFacts: Discovered in 2002 by the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research and named for Yuri Oganessian.
